correctness.rationale: For every queried edge support, integer outdegree-orientation feasibility yields the exact cut criterion. A degree-three vertex/cut argument establishes the seven-point VC upper bound, with explicit K4 disjoint K3 lower support. A complete 2047-node depth-eleven binary tree specifies 2048 distinct regular tournament leaf witnesses, independently checked against all 2640 enumerated regular tournaments; 2640<4096 forbids depth twelve. Two independent exact verifiers reproduce all 2,097,152 static support cut decisions and smaller-order checks. No infinite Littlestone inference is asserted.

originality.rationale: The genuinely new assessed assertion is the seven-vertex regular-tournament Littlestone dimension 11, first strict odd-order adaptive/static gap of two, and all intermediate seven-vertex shattered-support counts. Brualdi–Kiernan and the previously established all-odd-order static VC theorem already imply the static dimension and extremal nine-edge supports; those are explicitly credited and excluded from the novelty claim. Source-level primary comparisons and semantic-result searches did not find the eleven-level claim or entire support polynomial. This is a best-knowledge priority assessment, not proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: The natural class of orientations of a complete graph under constant score constraints has an explicit first static/adaptive shattering separation at seven vertices: VC=9, Ldim=11. The 2048-leaf adaptive witness and complete fixed-query support polynomial quantify the structural difference; the intermediate counts are not determined by the previously known maximal-support characterization. The result is limited but motivated by online learning of score-constrained orientations, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
